beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Captured Internet asks why a functioning network can become less worth entering.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Messages arrive while the rules governing attention escape the people living under them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book traces how useful platforms acquired power over identity, memory, and relevance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its proposed direction is governable networks with meaningful rights of voice and exit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That requires institutions above open protocols, rather than nostalgia for an innocent early web.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The argument connects community governance, personal recommendation, and the architecture of communication.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading it means asking who can change the rules of your digital life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The historical chapters explain why people entered platforms instead of treating their users as foolish.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Convenience, discovery, identity, and reliable service solved real coordination problems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Communities then invested relationships, moderation, knowledge, and memory inside those useful arrangements.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The provider could own the infrastructure while acquiring authority over the community’s future.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Leaving a service became harder when leaving also meant losing accumulated social life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This distinction connects the book’s history to its constructive institutional argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reading question becomes which useful services require ownership of the people depending on them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed alternative gives a community an existence apart from any single service provider.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A shared name can carry standards while different hosts provide compatible infrastructure.
